extracted.intended_audience: operators of public water systems, state drinking water regulators, and environmental testing laboratories
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures for inorganic chemical and turbidity sampling, analysis, reporting, confirmation, waivers, and compliance determination for public water systems under EPA Part 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total coliform MCL exceedance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system which has exceeded the MCL for total coliforms in § 141.63 must report the violation to the State no later than the end of the next business day after it learns of the violation, and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring violation reporting timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system which has failed to comply with a coliform monitoring requirement, including the sanitary survey requirement, must report the monitoring violation to the State within ten days after the system discovers the violation, and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity sampling frequency and representative entry points
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples shall be taken by suppliers of water for both community and non-community water systems at a representative entry point(s) to the water distribution system at least once per day, for the purposes of making turbidity measurements to determine compliance with § 141.13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State determines that a reduced sampling frequency in a non-community will not pose a risk to public health, it can reduce the required sampling frequency. The option to reduce turbidity frequency is permitted only in systems that practice disinfection and maintain an active residual disinfectant in the distribution system and where the State indicates in writing that no unreasonable risk to health exists. Turbidity measurements shall be made as directed in § 141.74(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity exceedance confirmation and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the result of a turbidity analysis indicates that the maximum allowable limit has been exceeded, the sampling and measurement shall be confirmed by resampling as soon as practicable and preferably within one hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the repeat sample confirms that the maximum allowable limit has been exceeded, the supplier must report to the State within 48 hours. The repeat sample shall be used for calculating the monthly average. If the monthly average exceeds the maximum allowable limit, or if the average of two samples on consecutive days exceeds 5 TU, the supplier must report to the State and notify the public per § 141.31 and subpart Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inorganic chemical monitoring requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Community, non-transient non-community, and transient non-community water systems shall conduct monitoring to determine compliance with the maximum contaminant levels specified in § 141.62 in accordance with this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling point selection and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater systems shall take a minimum of one sample at every entry point to the distribution system which is representative of each well after treatment. Surface water systems shall take a minimum of one sample at every entry point to the distribution system after any application of treatment or at a point representative of each source after treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system shall take each sample at the same sampling point unless conditions make another point more representative of the source or treatment plant. For combined sources, sample when water is representative of all sources being used (normal operating conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite sampling rules and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may reduce the number of samples by allowing compositing of a maximum of five samples provided the detection limit of the method used is less than one-fifth of the MCL; compositing must be done in the laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the concentration in the composite sample is ≥ one-fifth of the MCL for any inorganic chemical, a follow-up sample must be taken within 14 days at each sampling point included in the composite and analyzed for the contaminants which exceeded one-fifth of the MCL. If population served >3,300, compositing may only be permitted at sampling points within a single system; systems serving ≤3,300 may composite among different systems provided the 5-sample limit is maintained. If duplicates of the original sample are available, duplicates may be used instead of resampling provided holding times are not exceeded and results are reported to the State within 14 days after analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection limits and approved analytical methods (table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection limits for each analytical method and MCLs for each inorganic contaminant are specified in the table (lists contaminants, MCLs, methodologies, and detection limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis for contaminants shall be conducted in accordance with the methods in the table, or the alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C, or their equivalent as determined by EPA. Technical Notes on Drinking Water Methods contains criteria for analyzing certain contaminants and other analytical test procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asbestos monitoring frequency and waiver criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community and non-transient, non-community water system is required to monitor for asbestos during the first three-year compliance period of each nine-year compliance cycle beginning in the compliance period starting January 1, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system may apply to the State for a waiver if it believes it is not vulnerable to asbestos contamination from source water or corrosion of asbestos-cement pipe. The State may grant a waiver based on consideration of potential asbestos contamination of the source and the use/corrosiveness of asbestos-cement pipe. A waiver remains in effect until the completion of the three-year compliance period. Systems vulnerable due solely to corrosion must take one sample at a tap served by asbestos-cement pipe under likely contamination conditions; vulnerability due to source water follows paragraph (a) provisions. Systems exceeding the MCL shall monitor quarterly beginning in the next quarter; the State may decrease quarterly monitoring if system is reliably and consistently below MCL but only after minimum sample counts (groundwater: 2 quarterly; surface/combined: 4 quarterly) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency and waiver process for specified inorganics
rubrics_metrics.description: For antimony, arsenic, barium, beryllium, cadmium, chromium, cyanide, fluoride, mercury, nickel, selenium and thallium: groundwater systems shall take one sample at each sampling point during each compliance period; surface water systems shall take one sample annually at each sampling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system may apply for a waiver; a waiver requires at least one sample while effective and may not exceed one compliance cycle (nine years). The State may grant a waiver if surface systems have monitored annually for ≥3 years and groundwater systems have ≥3 rounds of monitoring with all previous results <MCL; new sources are ineligible until three rounds completed. In determining reduced frequency the State shall consider reported concentrations, degree of variation, and other factors affecting contaminant concentrations (e.g., pumping rates, system configuration, operating procedures, stream flows). State waiver decisions shall be in writing and set forth the basis. Systems exceeding the MCL shall monitor quarterly beginning next quarter; State may decrease quarterly monitoring only after minimum quarterly samples have been taken (groundwater: 2; surface: 4). New systems or systems using a new source after Jan 22, 2004 must demonstrate compliance within a State-specified time and follow initial sampling frequencies specified by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nitrate monitoring frequency and repeat monitoring rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All public water systems shall monitor to determine compliance with the maximum contaminant level for nitrate in § 141.62. Community and non-transient non-community groundwater systems shall monitor annually beginning Jan 1, 1993; systems served by surface water shall monitor quarterly beginning Jan 1, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat monitoring frequency for groundwater systems shall be quarterly for at least one year following any sample ≥50% of the MCL. The State may allow groundwater systems to reduce to annual after four consecutive quarterly samples reliably and consistently less than the MCL. The State may allow surface water systems to reduce to annual if four consecutive quarters are <50% of the MCL; surface systems return to quarterly if any sample is ≥50% of the MCL. Each transient non-community system shall monitor annually. After initial quarterly sampling, systems monitoring annually shall take subsequent samples during the quarter(s) which previously resulted in the highest analytical result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nitrite monitoring frequency and repeat monitoring rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All public water systems shall monitor to determine compliance with the maximum contaminant level for nitrite in § 141.62(b). All public water systems shall take one sample at each sampling point in the compliance period beginning Jan 1, 1993 and ending Dec 31, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the initial sample, systems with nitrite <50% of the MCL shall monitor at the frequency specified by the State. Repeat monitoring frequency for any water system shall be quarterly for at least one year following any sample ≥50% of the MCL; the State may allow reduction to annual after determining system is reliably and consistently less than the MCL. Annual-monitoring systems shall take subsequent samples during the quarter(s) which previously resulted in the highest analytical result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation sample timing for metal and complex contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: Where results of sampling for antimony, arsenic, asbestos, barium, beryllium, cadmium, chromium, cyanide, fluoride, mercury, nickel, selenium or thallium indicate an exceedance of the MCL, the State may require that one additional sample be collected as soon as possible after the initial sample was taken (but not to exceed two weeks) at the same sampling point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation sample timing and procedures for nitrate and nitrite
rubrics_metrics.description: Where nitrate or nitrite sampling results indicate an exceedance of the MCL, the system shall take a confirmation sample within 24 hours of the system's receipt of notification of the analytical results of the first sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems unable to comply with the 24-hour requirement must immediately notify persons served in accordance with § 141.202 and meet Tier 1 public notification requirements under subpart Q. Systems exercising this option must take and analyze a confirmation sample within two weeks of notification of the analytical results of the first sample. If a State-required confirmation sample is taken for any contaminant, the results of the initial and confirmation sample shall be averaged; the resulting average shall be used to determine compliance. States have discretion to delete results of obvious sampling errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority to require more frequent monitoring and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may require more frequent monitoring than specified in paragraphs (b), (c), (d) and (e) or may require confirmation samples for positive and negative results at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: System-initiated increased monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may apply to the State to conduct more frequent monitoring than the minimum monitoring frequencies specified in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determination and averaging rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with § 141.11 or § 141.62(b) shall be determined based on the analytical result(s) obtained at each sampling point with specific rules depending on monitoring frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems monitoring at a frequency greater than annual, compliance for the specified inorganics is determined by a running annual average at any sampling point; if the average at any point is greater than the MCL, the system is out of compliance. Any one sample that would cause the annual average to be exceeded results in immediate noncompliance. Any sample below the method detection limit (MDL) shall be calculated at zero for the purpose of determining the annual average. If a system fails to collect the required number of samples, compliance will be based on the total number of samples collected. For systems monitoring annually or less frequently, a system is out of compliance if the contaminant level is greater than the MCL; if confirmation samples are required the determination will be based on the annual average of the initial MCL exceedance and any State-required confirmation samples. For nitrate/nitrite, compliance is determined based on one sample if levels are below the MCL; if initial sample exceeds the MCL a confirmation sample is required and compliance shall be determined based on the average of the initial and confirmation samples. Arsenic sampling results will be reported to the nearest 0.001 mg/L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring timing per State schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public water system shall monitor at the time designated by the State during each compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved analytical methods and incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis for contaminants shall be conducted in accordance with the methods listed in the methods table, or alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C, or their equivalent as determined by EPA; numerous EPA, ASTM, and Standard Methods references are incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical Notes on Drinking Water Methods (EPA-600/R-94-173) contains additional criteria and is available from NSCEP. Copies of referenced documents may be obtained from the listed sources or inspected at EPA's Drinking Water Docket or NARA. The incorporation by reference of specified documents was approved by the Director of the Federal Register in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51.
